questions.text: Which accessibility concept is source-safe from the checked BP 344 2024 IRR?

options.text: An accessible route is continuous, unobstructed, and connects accessible elements so persons with disabilities can negotiate it safely and independently.
An accessible route may include stairs and turnstiles if signs are posted.
An accessible route is only an exterior driveway.
An accessible route is optional when the building is privately owned.

questions.rationale: BP 344 defines an accessible route as a continuous unobstructed path connecting accessible elements and spaces, excluding steps, stairways, turnstiles, revolving doors, escalators, and similar impediments.

questions.text: Which BP 344 2024 ramp requirement is supported by the checked source?

options.text: Accessible ramps have a minimum clear width of 1200 mm and gradient not steeper than 1:20, except special cases stated by the source.
Accessible ramps may be 700 mm wide for public-use buildings.
A ramp is never required for a change in level.
Accessible ramps do not need landings.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 ramp text states the minimum clear width and general gradient rule, and also lists landing and handrail features.
questions.explanation: This question tests BO personal liability — both administrative (CSC/Ombudsman) and criminal (PD 1096 Sec. 213) — for knowingly issuing permits for non-compliant buildings.

questions.text: What handrail height is source-safe for accessible ramps and stairs under BP 344 2024?

options.text: Handrails at 900 mm and 700 mm above ramps and stairs.
One handrail at 1200 mm only.
Handrails only at landings, not along ramps.
No handrails when a ramp has tactile blocks.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 states that handrails shall be installed at 900 mm and 700 mm above ramps and stairs.
questions.explanation: This foundational question tests the critical distinction between the Building Official (permit authority) and DPWH (rule-making authority) — one of the most common LEA traps.

questions.text: What accessible parking dimension is supported by the checked BP 344 2024 source?

options.text: A minimum width of 4000 mm and length of 5000 mm.
A minimum width of 2400 mm and length of 4200 mm.
The same size as an ordinary parking slot without access aisle.
Only the number of slots is regulated, not the size.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 parking text states that accessible parking slots have a minimum width of 4000 mm and length of 5000 mm.
questions.explanation: This application question tests the COO-accessibility link — the COO cannot be issued unless all accessibility features from the approved plans are physically present.

questions.text: Which statement about accessible parking location is source-safe under BP 344 2024?

options.text: Accessible parking slots are located nearest accessible main entrances or close to accessible elevators/pedestrian entrances in parking structures.
Accessible parking should be placed in sloping ramped areas.
Accessible parking location is unrelated to accessible routes.
Accessible parking must always be farthest from entrances.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 requires accessible parking to be near accessible entrances and forbids locating PWD parking slots in ramped or sloping areas.
questions.explanation: This understanding question addresses the most common scope misconception — that private buildings are exempt from BP 344. The coverage test is public access, not ownership.

questions.text: Which BP 344 signage statement is supported by the checked source?

options.text: Directional signs with the International Symbol of Access lead persons with disabilities to facilities such as elevators, entrances, toilets, and parking.
Accessible signage is required only in parking areas.
Signs may protrude into corridors without clearance limits.
Braille signage is never mentioned.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 signage provisions require the International Symbol of Access and directional signs to accessible facilities.
questions.explanation: This question tests the DPWH role — specifically that it sets rules and inspects but does NOT issue building permits, which remains the BO's exclusive function.

questions.text: What is source-safe for accessible elevator cars in the checked BP 344 2024 source?

options.text: Minimum depth 1400 mm, width 1500 mm, and clear door opening width at least 900 mm.
Minimum depth 900 mm and width 900 mm.
Only stairs are preferred vertical access.
Elevator dimensions are not addressed.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 lists accessible elevator car depth, width, and clear door opening width.
questions.explanation: This application question tests the correct second step in the BP 344 enforcement escalation chain — DPWH Regional Office — not PRC, HLURB, or courts at this stage.

questions.text: What does BP 344 2024 say about public-use buildings?

options.text: They are structures accessible to the general public, whether privately or publicly owned, with spaces available for communal use.
Only national government buildings are public-use buildings.
Privately owned malls can never be public-use buildings.
Only residential dwellings are public-use buildings.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 definition includes structures accessible to the general public whether privately or publicly owned.
questions.explanation: This evaluation question tests the architect's non-delegable duty under RA 9266 — the professional must refuse non-compliant work regardless of client instructions, with withdrawal as the ultimate recourse.

questions.text: What area-of-refuge statement is supported by BP 344 2024?

options.text: It is a fire-separated area with direct access to an exit where persons unable to use stairs may temporarily await assistance, with minimum space per non-ambulant person.
It is a storage room used for furniture.
It is a parking aisle.
It replaces all required exits.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 definition describes an area of refuge as separated, exit-connected, and intended for temporary safety during emergency evacuation.
questions.explanation: This analysis question tests the 'continuing violation' doctrine — that active accessibility failures have no prescriptive clock because the violation resets daily — a critical enforcement concept.

questions.text: Which source-safe rule applies to accessible transport pathways and corridors?

options.text: Accessible pathways and corridors along the passenger path have a minimum width of 1800 mm, with at least 900 mm clearance at barriers.
All corridors may narrow to 600 mm at columns.
Pathway widths are not addressed in BP 344.
Escalators alone complete an accessible passenger route.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 sets a minimum accessible pathway/corridor width along passenger paths and a clearance where barriers are present.
questions.explanation: This analysis question tests simultaneous liability — architect (design) and owner (construction/maintenance/operation) are independently liable and neither shields the other.
questions.code_citation: BP 344; RA 9266; RA 10754; Civil Code Art. 2176

questions.text: Which source-safe answer fits a privately owned shopping mall open to the public?

options.text: It can fall within BP 344 public-use building coverage because public-use buildings may be privately or publicly owned.
It is excluded because private ownership always removes public-use status.
It is governed only by tax discount rules in this batch.
It is automatically exempt from accessible routes.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 defines public-use buildings as accessible to the general public whether privately or publicly owned.
questions.explanation: This question tests the 10-year civil liability period under RA 9266 — which is specific to architects and differs from the general 4-year quasi-delict period under the Civil Code.
